claim: Legal section: "New Jersey has not enacted an employer-facing biometric privacy statute" is marked confirmed:true and sourced to the A3929 bill text.
problem: The cited page is the text of a pending consumer-facing bill; it says nothing about whether an employer-facing biometric statute exists or not. The negative is probably true but is unsupported by the cited source, yet it is presented as confirmed.
fix: Re-source the absence claim to a page that actually states it (e.g. the recordinglaw.com New Jersey biometric-privacy page), or reword to "no employer-facing New Jersey biometric statute was identified in this session" and mark it as research finding rather than confirmed rule.

claim: Legal section, "Documented hygiene monitoring duty and bare-hand contact": the N.J.A.C. 8:24-8.13 inspection-report-on-premises rule (most recent report kept for public review, at least two years) is cited to the 8:24-3.3 URL.
problem: The rule is real - I confirmed it verbatim - but it is not on the cited page. 8:24-3.3 contains only the hand/bare-hand-contact provisions, so the citation does not support the sentence it is attached to.
fix: Add a separate citation to https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/new-jersey/N-J-A-C-8-24-8-13 for the 8.13 sentence (keep 8:24-3.3 for the (a)2/(a)4 sentence).

claim: Pilot cost_range: "Roughly $4,000-9,000 one-time per site", built from "hardware about $1,300-2,000" plus "40-70 hours ... at $75-125/hour = $3,000-8,750".
problem: The stated range does not follow from its own components: $1,300-2,000 + $3,000-8,750 = $4,300-10,750. Both the bottom ($4,000) and top ($9,000) of the published range are inconsistent with the arithmetic. The $150-400/month ongoing figure is also not derived from anything in the section.
fix: Restate as $4,300-10,750 one-time (or round to $4,500-11,000), and show one line of arithmetic for the monthly figure (e.g. support hours + hosting) or mark it explicitly as an unanchored estimate.

claim: Miso Flippy: "Vision-guided robot that dispenses, fries and baskets fries at roughly 100 baskets/hour".
problem: The press release says the new Flippy "can process more than 100 baskets per hour - almost twice as many as humans". "Roughly 100" understates and drops the "more than" qualifier.
fix: Change to "more than 100 baskets per hour (vendor claim, nearly twice human throughput)".

claim: KITRO is described as "the device used in the 2025 peer-reviewed HORECA trial".
problem: ReFED's summary (the source actually read) describes five foodservice sites in Germany, Greece and Switzerland and does not use the term HORECA; the "HORECA" label is imported and unverified.
fix: Say "the device used in the five-site 2025 European foodservice study summarised by ReFED (May 2026)".
